label: First day at school

what_happens.title: What happens on the first day
goals: School is a place to play, learn and make things with other children
The day has parts in order: goodbye, circle time, play, snack, outside, pick-up
The grown-up comes back at the end of the day
what_happens.parentSkill: Walk through the school day in order and let your child say which part comes next.

who_is_there.title: Who is at school
goals: The teacher's job is to keep children safe and help them learn
Other children are new too, and friends can take a few days
The child can say hello and ask to play
who_is_there.parentSkill: Practise one sentence for joining in: 'Hi, can I play too?'

what_i_do.title: What I do at school
goals: A special goodbye that is always the same
Asking the teacher for the bathroom, water or help
Hanging up the coat and finding a spot
what_i_do.parentSkill: Make a short goodbye ritual together and keep it the same every morning.

if_scared.title: If I feel sad or scared
goals: Missing a grown-up is normal and the feeling gets smaller
Loud rooms and new things can feel big; a quiet corner and slow breaths help
Teachers help when something goes wrong
if_scared.parentSkill: Say goodbye once, warmly and briefly, and never sneak away.

rehearsal.title: Let's practise school
goals: Play school at home with a toy teacher
Practise the goodbye and saying hello
Go through the whole day once more, ending with pick-up
rehearsal.parentSkill: Let your child be the teacher and you be the new kid.

steps: Walk to the school door with a grown-up
Have a special goodbye hug at the door
Hang up the coat and find a spot in the classroom
Circle time on the rug, then play time
Snack time and time outside on the playground
The grown-up comes back at pick-up time
sensory: the smell of snacks and paint
a soft rug for circle time
a bell or a song that means 'tidy up'
honestyNotes: Some children cry at goodbye and that is normal. Never promise the child will not feel sad or will make a friend on day one. Promise only what is true: the grown-up comes back.

fallbackAnswer: Yes. [[GROWNUP]] always comes back at pick-up time.
While you play and learn, [[GROWNUP]] is thinking about you.

questionButtons.text: What if nobody plays with me?
fallbackAnswer: It can take a few days to find a friend, and that's okay.
You can say, hi, can I play too? The teacher can help you find a game.

questionButtons.text: What if I need the toilet?
fallbackAnswer: You can tell your teacher, I need the bathroom.
Teachers help children with that every day. It's a good thing to ask.
The teacher's job is to help children and keep them safe.
You can say good morning, and the teacher will say it back.

questionButtons.text: What will I do all day?
fallbackAnswer: There is circle time, play time, snack time and time outside.
Then [[GROWNUP]] comes to pick you up.
Classrooms can get loud when everyone plays.
You can tell the teacher and sit somewhere quiet for a little while.

techniques.label: A special goodbye
techniques.how: Pick one short goodbye, for example a hug, a high five and 'see you at pick-up', and keep it the same every morning.

techniques.label: A heart on the hand
techniques.how: Draw a small heart on your child's hand and on yours; pressing it means 'I'm thinking of you'.

techniques.label: Practising 'Can I play too?'
techniques.how: Practise one sentence for joining a game, and role-play it with toys.

techniques.label: Asking the teacher
techniques.how: Practise asking: 'I need the bathroom', 'Can you help me?'. Tell the teacher anything your child needs.

techniques.label: A picture schedule of the day
techniques.how: Draw the parts of the day in order and look at them together at breakfast.

techniques.label: A quiet corner break
techniques.how: Ask the teacher whether your child can sit somewhere quiet when the room gets loud.

techniques.label: Smell the flower, blow the candle
techniques.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose like smelling a flower and out like blowing a candle.

ritual: A goodbye hug at the door

separation: I always come back. I'll be here at pick-up time.
When you miss me, press the heart on your hand.
social: It can take a few days to make friends, and that's okay.
You can say: 'Hi, can I play too?'
body: You can always tell the teacher: 'I need the bathroom.'
Asking for help is a big-kid thing to do.
strangers: Your teacher's job is to help you and keep you safe.
Let's say good morning to the teacher together.
unknown: First goodbye, then circle time, play and snack, then I pick you up.
Let's look at the picture of your day.
sensory: If it gets loud, you can ask for a quiet spot.
It's okay to cover your ears when it gets loud.
safety: Teachers keep children safe at school.
If something feels wrong, tell the teacher right away.
pain: If you fall down, a teacher will help you.
It's okay to cry if something hurts. Grown-ups at school will help.
love: I love you all day, even when we're apart.

sentences.text: Soon [[CHILD]] will start school.
School is a place where children play, learn and make things together.
First, [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] walk to the school door.
Then there is a big goodbye hug.
Next, [[CHILD]] hangs up a coat and finds a spot in the classroom.
Then the day goes step by step.
There is circle time, when everyone sits on a rug and sings.
There is play time with blocks, books and paint.
There is snack time and time outside on the playground.
After that, [[GROWNUP]] comes back to pick [[CHILD]] up.
At the door, a teacher says good morning.
The teacher's job is to keep every child safe and help them learn.
There may be a helper teacher in the room too.
[[CHILD]] can wave and say hello.
The teacher waves back with a big smile.
Teachers love the first day of school.
There are other children in the classroom too.
Some are new, just like [[CHILD]].
Some children talk a lot, and some are quiet at first.
It can take a few days to find a friend.
[[CHILD]] can say, hi, do you want to play?
In the morning, [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] have a special goodbye.
A big hug, a high five, and a heart drawn on [[CHILD]]'s hand.
When [[CHILD]] misses [[GROWNUP]], [[CHILD]] can press the heart.
Then [[GROWNUP]] goes, and comes back at pick-up time.
At school, [[CHILD]] can ask for help any time.
If [[CHILD]] needs the toilet, [[CHILD]] can tell the teacher, I need the bathroom.
If [[CHILD]] is thirsty or tired, the teacher can help with that too.
Asking is a big-kid job, and teachers like it.
Sometimes [[CHILD]] may feel sad when [[GROWNUP]] leaves.
Lots of children cry a little on the first days, and that is okay.
The teacher will help, and the sad feeling gets smaller.
[[GROWNUP]] always comes back.
[[CHILD]] can press the heart on the hand and take a slow breath.
The classroom can be loud when everyone plays at once.
If the noise feels too big, [[CHILD]] can tell the teacher and sit in a quiet corner for a little while.
If [[CHILD]] falls down outside, a teacher helps.
Grown-ups at school keep children safe.
Tonight [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] play school at home.
A toy is the teacher and says good morning.
They practise the special goodbye: a hug, a high five and a heart on the hand.
Then the toy says, I'll come back after snack time.
And the toy does come back.
Let's say the school day once more.
First, the goodbye hug at the door.
Then circle time, play time and snack time.
Next, time outside on the playground.
After that, [[GROWNUP]] comes back to pick [[CHILD]] up.
[[GROWNUP]] loves hearing all about the day.
